notes: User revision v7: exclude North 1NT with a five-card minor, unless spades contain A, KQ, or QJ in at least four cards, when HCP6-8 OR 5422 OR that five-card minor contains at least two of AKQJ. All v6 filters otherwise unchanged.
User revision v6: four spades qualify for proactive penalty at single-suit full KnR >=5.65, total HCP >=8, and a side A/K.
User revision v6: five spades qualify at single-suit full KnR >=6.25 with total HCP >=8; total HCP >=7 suffices when spades contain A or both K and Q.

User revision v6 monotonicity: five spades also qualify if deleting any one spade yields a qualifying four-spade evaluation. Subtract the deleted honor HCP and retain all side suits. This is an evaluation projection, not a dealt 12-card hand.
The proposed alternative five-spade threshold 5.50 and a separate sequence override were not adopted. Use the last explicit 6.25 requirement plus four-to-five inheritance.

KnR is quality (steps1-12) plus high-card components (steps13-23) for this suit only; no allocation of whole-hand adjustments. Source https://www.rpbridge.net/8j19.htm; corrected step8 requires neither 8 nor T.
V6 replaces the old trump-promotion penalty criterion. Promotion floor remains diagnostic only. No filtering uses DD or Par outcomes.
User revision v5: at 15+ HCP East has extra strength and may need to rebid 2H even with poor four-card hearts. Heart quality alone never excludes these hands.

No general weak-four-heart exclusion. In particular 5S4H with 15-17 HCP remains eligible regardless of heart honors, subject to the other agreed rules.
The 5422 strong-NT opening style is unresolved: retain 15-17 HCP hands with honors in both minor doubletons in the primary sample, and report a separate sensitivity analysis omitting them.
